s_last.speaker: SYLVIE
lines: Door seventeen. Two knocks, a breath, one knock — you saw it. From here the city is not mine; Madame Béranger owns the air you breathe now, and she counts every litre of it.
Here. Seventeen. You saw the knock. Past this door I am nobody again — the woman inside owns the air in her rooms, and she is owed for all of it.

s_advice.speaker: SYLVIE
lines: One thing for nothing, American. In the country, danger looks like a uniform. In the city it looks like a favour. Weigh every kindness.
Free advice, the last thing free in Paris: out here the dangerous men wear uniforms. In there, they bring bread and ask after your mother. Weigh every kindness.

choices.text: Thank you. For every field between here and the barn.

s_bye.speaker: SYLVIE
lines: Thank the fields. They did the hiding; I only walked in front of you. Go — the breath between the knocks is not a poem, it is a clock.
Keep the thanks for after the war; they spend better then. Go on. Knock the way you saw.

s_no.speaker: SYLVIE
lines: If you see me again and we are lucky, we will not know each other. That is the trade. Go — knock the way you saw.
If our luck holds, never. If you do see me, walk past me. Now knock.

s_nod.speaker: SYLVIE
lines: There he is. Jean Caillet, who says nothing and survives everything. Knock.
A nod. Keep that man; he is the one they cannot catch talking. Go.
